passage: Yuvan's model house was due at the end of the week, and he had a big plan: windows, a balcony, a garden, blue paint. On Monday, after school in the art room, he made just a plain box from a cereal carton with a flat cardboard roof glued on top. It looked a bit bare. "Show it to Rajni Ma'am anyway," he told himself. She turned it around slowly. "Steady work. The roof sits straight. What comes next?" Yuvan pointed at the empty walls. "Windows." On Tuesday he cut four windows. On Wednesday he painted the walls yellow. By Friday a small balcony stood at the front, and the house was done, with every step already checked.

qa.a: Yuvan first made a plain box with a flat cardboard roof glued on top.

qa.q: How did Yuvan feel about the first plain box?
qa.a: Yuvan felt it looked a bit bare and may have been unsure, but he showed it to the teacher anyway.

qa.q: What could Yuvan do if the teacher suggested a different roof shape?
qa.a: Yuvan could change the roof early while the model is still simple, which is easier than fixing it after the paint is done.

qa.q: How might Rajni see Yuvan's early showing?
qa.a: Rajni may be pleased that Yuvan asked early, since comments can shape the model while it is easy to change.

passage:
"Just a box?" Sachin asked, looking at Eshaan's desk.
"With a roof," Eshaan said, pointing to the folded card on top. "It's version one. I'm showing Ma'am tomorrow."
"Where are the windows?"
"Later. First I want to know if the size is right and if the roof stays on." Eshaan pressed the roof. It held.
The next day he came home smiling. "Ma'am said the size is good, but the roof should slope more so it looks like a real house."
Wednesday he fixed the roof. Thursday, two windows and a door. Saturday, red paint and a white door.
Sachin looked at it. "Okay. That's actually nice."
"See? If I'd painted it first, I'd have had to redo everything when the roof was wrong."

qa.q: What did Eshaan add to the house on Saturday?
qa.a: Red paint and a white door.

qa.q: How did Eshaan feel coming home after showing Ma'am?
qa.a: He felt happy and encouraged, since she said the size was good and gave him one clear thing to fix.

qa.q: Why was building a simple box first a good choice?
qa.a: Because the teacher could check the size and roof early, so Eshaan fixed those before spending time on windows and paint.

qa.q: How does Sachin see the model at first and at the end?
qa.a: Sachin first thinks it's just a box, but by Saturday admits the finished house is actually nice.

grounding: It shows a boy building a plain box with a roof first, showing his teacher, and adding windows and paint on later days.

passage:
I'm Santosh, and for the school craft fair I had to make a model house.
My cousin Nilesh wanted to start with the fun parts: a balcony, curtains, a garden. But I was worried. What if it didn't stand up?
So on Monday I made only a plain box from an old shoe carton, with a folded roof. I showed Sir. He said the walls were fine but the roof was too heavy.
Tuesday, a lighter roof. Wednesday, windows. Thursday, Nilesh helped me paint it yellow and add a moss garden.
At the fair, my roof stayed on all day. A girl's model next to mine had a beautiful balcony, but its roof fell in by lunch.
I felt a bit sorry for her. And quite proud of my boring box.

qa.q: What did Santosh make the box from?
How did Santosh feel at the end of the fair?
qa.a: Santosh felt quite proud of the simple start and a bit sorry for the girl whose roof fell in.

qa.q: What else could Santosh do in the next project?
qa.a: Santosh could again show a simple first version early, so any big problem is found before the decorating starts.

qa.q: How might Nilesh see the plan to start with a plain box?
qa.a: Nilesh wanted to begin with the fun parts, so may have found it boring at first, but still got to help with the garden later.
